Declare a distance decay kernel

Source: R/01-decay_kernel.R
decay_kernel.Rd

Declares the decay weights \(w(d; \sigma)\) that calc_decay() and the FCA functions apply to a travel time or distance \(d\). A declaration is plain data: it names a built-in kernel, or it records your own function as the exact text of its code (comments and layout are not kept), together with what its parameter sigma means, the bounds sigma may take and any fixed extra arguments. Nothing but data is stored, so a declaration can be compared, saved and reloaded in a fresh session. This experimental function lets one declaration be used wherever a decay method is accepted. A declaration can also be passed as family to clm_allocation().

Usage

decay_kernel(
  fun,
  name = NULL,
  parameter = NULL,
  lower = 0,
  upper = Inf,
  zero_distance = TRUE,
  smooth = TRUE,
  args = list()
)

# S3 method for class 'spax_decay_kernel'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

fun

A built-in kernel name ("gaussian", "exponential" or "power"), or a closure function(distance, sigma, ...) that returns the weights.

name

A single string naming a custom kernel. It starts with a letter and continues with letters, digits, _, . or -, and it is not (in any capitalization) gaussian, exponential, power, inverse, binary or none. Required for a function; not allowed for a built-in kernel.

parameter

A single nonempty string saying what sigma means for the kernel, for example "scale". It labels printed output. Required for a function.

lower, upper

Inclusive bounds on sigma, with 0 <= lower < upper <= Inf. Wherever the kernel is used, sigma must also be positive, so a lower of 0 allows any positive sigma but not 0 itself.

zero_distance

FALSE declares the kernel undefined at distance zero, as the power kernel is: the check at declaration then leaves zero out of its grid, and a model from clm_allocation() refuses prepared inputs that contain a finite zero travel time when it is evaluated or fitted.

smooth

FALSE declares a kernel that is not smooth in sigma (steps or thresholds). It can be evaluated, predicted and used in FCA: a model built with clm_allocation() can be evaluated at fixed parameters with evaluate_allocation() and used for requested-location prediction with predict_allocation(), but fit_allocation() refuses it, because model fitting and bootstrapping need a kernel that is smooth in sigma. Evaluate such a kernel at fixed parameters instead, for example over a grid of sigma and v0.

args

A named list of fixed extra arguments for fun. Its names must be arguments of fun other than distance and sigma; its values must be numeric, logical or character vectors without attributes.

x

A spax_decay_kernel.

...

Unused.

Value

A spax_decay_kernel: a list of plain data with the fields name, builtin, parameter, lower, upper, zero_distance, smooth, args and code (the exact text of the function's code, with comments and layout not kept; NA for a built-in kernel).

Details

Built-in kernels. decay_kernel("gaussian"), decay_kernel("exponential") and decay_kernel("power") declare the kernels of the same names in calc_decay(). They take no other argument and behave exactly like the method strings. Their sigma is a travel scale, a rate and an exponent; the power kernel is undefined at distance zero.

Your own function. fun must be a closure whose first two arguments are distance and sigma, and it must return one weight per distance. It must be elementwise: each distance gets its own weight, independent of the other distances, because it may receive a vector or a matrix of distances. Every other argument needs a default value, an entry in args, or is .... The function is stored as text and rebuilt in the base environment whenever it is used, so it may use only its arguments, base R, pkg::fn calls (for example stats::pnorm) and args. It cannot refer to objects in your workspace.

Checks at declaration. The function is run on a grid of distances (0.1 to 1000, and 0 unless zero_distance = FALSE) at a few values of sigma inside the bounds, including a positive lower and a finite upper bound themselves. Every call must return a numeric vector with one value per distance that is finite, nonnegative and non-increasing in distance, and the values must be identical whether the function is run from its stored text or as given. A function whose weight for a distance depends on the other distances is refused as well. A function that fails a check is refused with the reason.

Saving. The stored code is parsed, and turned into a function without running it, whenever the kernel is used; running the kernel runs that code. As with any R function, use declarations only from sources you trust. Fits, evaluations and predictions that use a declared kernel carry its code, and saveRDS() saves it with them. Using such a result again, for example to predict from it after readRDS(), runs that code, so read saved results only from sources you trust, as for any file that holds functions such as a loss function. To rebuild a model for a saved fit, take the declaration from the fit (fit$best$prediction_snapshot$spec$kernel) rather than declaring the function again, because the stored text can differ between R versions.

See also

Other allocation steps: bootstrap_fit(), calc_demand(), calc_travel_time(), check_fit(), clm_allocation(), compare_fits(), evaluate_allocation(), fit_allocation(), huff_allocation(), predict_allocation(), prepare_allocation()

Examples

# A built-in declaration behaves like its method string
decay_kernel("gaussian")
#> <spax_decay_kernel> gaussian (built-in)
#> sigma: travel scale
#> bounds on sigma: 0 to Inf
#> defined at distance 0: yes
#> smooth in sigma: yes
#> fixed arguments: none
#> function:
#> function (distance, sigma = 11.64884, ...) 
#> {
#>     return(exp(-(distance^2)/(2 * sigma^2)))
#> }

# A plateau kernel: full weight within 5 minutes, Gaussian decay beyond
plateau <- decay_kernel(
  function(distance, sigma, plateau = 5) {
    ifelse(distance <= plateau, 1, exp(-(distance - plateau)^2 / (2 * sigma^2)))
  },
  name = "plateau", parameter = "scale", args = list(plateau = 5)
)
plateau
#> <spax_decay_kernel> plateau
#> sigma: scale
#> bounds on sigma: 0 to Inf
#> defined at distance 0: yes
#> smooth in sigma: yes
#> fixed arguments: plateau = 5
#> function:
#> function (distance, sigma, plateau = 5) 
#> {
#>     ifelse(distance <= plateau, 1, exp(-(distance - plateau)^2/(2 * 
#>         sigma^2)))
#> }

calc_decay(c(0, 5, 10, 20, NA), plateau, sigma = 8)
#> [1] 1.0000000 1.0000000 0.8225776 0.1724216        NA
